DUK.thesis_one_line: Regulated Carolinas/Florida/Midwest utility growing rate base off data-center demand, priced for less growth than it is guiding to.
DUK.confidence_in_thesis: med (guidance reaffirmed and cross-checked against filed Q2 2026 10-Q, but no consolidated net-debt/EBITDA disclosed and a 2026-09-25 8-K was not opened)
kill_criteria: FY adjusted EPS guidance ($6.55-$6.80) is cut at any quarterly release (vs. reaffirmed/raised).

Consolidated long-term debt grows >8% in a single fiscal year without a matching equity/NCI raise (i.e., leverage build accelerates beyond the current run-rate - Jun-26 LT debt +2.7% over six months, +2.2% in the quarter [corrected by DV13]).
Two consecutive quarters of YoY adjusted EPS growth below 3% (below the low end of the long-term algorithm).
A credit-rating downgrade to BBB or equivalent (from current investment-grade BBB+/A- tier) by S&P or Moody's.
A major adverse rate-case order (disallowed capex >$500M in a single jurisdiction) in the Carolinas or Florida.
key_adverse_facts: H1 2026 free cash flow was negative (~-$3,968M): operating cash flow $4,272M vs capex $8,240M, financed by debt/NCI/asset sales.
Consolidated long-term debt rose from $80,108M (Dec-25) to $82,242M (Jun-26).
No consolidated net-debt/EBITDA figure is disclosed in the 10-Q; not independently reconstructed this cycle.
data_conflicts: None material vs the Q14 triage; quant snapshot's ~16x NTM P/E is consistent with this dossier's ~17.0x calc off guided FY2026 midpoint EPS.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Restated by verification DV13 (2026-10-06): original reverse dividend-growth DCF used rf 4.2% (UST was 5.17% on 25 Sep 2026), a 7.8% cost of equity and a perpetuity (~4.0%) vs a 5-7% growth range. At 8.4-8.7% cost of equity a two-stage test (3% terminal) implies ~7.0-7.7%/yr 10-year growth, at or above the top of guidance, i.e. in_line (not below); base scenario return +8%/yr ~ cost of equity. No V1 row exists for DUK.

DUK.scenario_basis: Base: FY2026 guided adjusted EPS midpoint $6.675, ~6%/yr guided growth, ~3.8% dividend yield, roughly flat 17x multiple. Bear: growth slows to ~3% (regulatory lag/rate-case friction) with multiple compression to ~14x. Bull: data-center load growth pushes growth to ~8% with multiple expansion to ~19x. Cost-of-equity assumption 7.8% throughout (analyst estimate, not filed).
DUK.dv13_correction: Verdict INCLUDE -> INCLUDE-SMALL on valuation restatement; LT debt +2.7% was over six months (+2.2% in the quarter); total debt incl. current maturities and CP is $91.2bn. Post-10-Q 8-K of 2026-08-13: $2.0bn equity units (40m x $50) = future equity issuance. See dossiers/DUK.md Correction (verification DV13, 2026-10-06).

ERIE.thesis_one_line: Manages Erie Insurance Exchange for a capped, debt-free management fee with excellent ROE, but the fee itself is under an escalating legal challenge.
ERIE.confidence_in_thesis: med (financials cross-checked to the filed 10-Q; litigation timeline read directly from the 10-Q's own Legal Proceedings note, but the current Allegheny County docket status was not independently pulled)
kill_criteria: Any court order or settlement that reduces the effective management fee rate below the current ~25% cap, retroactively or prospectively.
Management-fee revenue growth (policy issuance + renewal + administrative) falls below 2% YoY for two consecutive quarters (vs. +4.5-4.7% in H1 2026).
Commission + non-commission cost of operations grows faster than management-fee revenue for three consecutive quarters.
A verdict or settlement in Stephenson (or the amended June 2026 complaint) that establishes actual damages or a refund obligation, of any size.
Dividend payout ratio rises above 60% without a corresponding acceleration in fee growth (vs. ~41% currently).
key_adverse_facts: Amended Complaint filed 2026-06-11 in the Court of Common Pleas of Allegheny County expands the challenged management-fee period to calendar years 2020-to-present (previously just 2019-2020), after Erie lost at the Third Circuit (2025-10-14) and the Supreme Court declined cert (2026-03-23).
Commission expense grew faster than management-fee revenue in Q2 2026 (+$44.7M vs +$39.0M fee growth), a margin item to watch.
Revenue base is fully dependent on a separate legal entity (Erie Insurance Exchange) that ERIE does not own - a structural concentration.
data_conflicts: The Q05 triage described the litigation as SCOTUS having 'declined to review, so the case proceeds' at the Third Circuit stage; this dossier finds the case has since moved to state court and the plaintiffs' scope has grown (June 2026 amendment) - an update, not a contradiction, but materially more adverse than the triage's framing.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: DV15 restated: no V1 row. Dividend-only Gordon is not the programme method (41% payout). TTM free cash flow ~$553M (OCF $697.8M less capex $144.7M) is a 4.7% yield; at Ke ~8.1% (UST 5.17% + ~0.7 x 4.14%) implied perpetual growth is ~3.2% vs 4.5-5.5% delivered: priced below the base case; litigation tail (Amended Complaint 11 Jun 2026) is the reason for half weight.

ERIE.scenario_basis: Base: ~5-6% fee/EPS growth, ~2.3% dividend yield, stable ~20x multiple. Bear: adverse litigation development (fee reduction risk or growth deceleration) derates multiple to ~16x. Bull: litigation dismissed/settled favorably and Exchange premium growth stays strong, multiple expands to ~23x. Cost-of-equity assumption 8.0% throughout (analyst estimate, not filed).

PHM.thesis_one_line: Move-up and active-adult homebuilder at a trough-cycle P/E, but it funded buybacks partly with new debt this half while cash flow fell.
PHM.confidence_in_thesis: med (financials cross-checked to the filed 10-Q; no formal company guidance exists to track, and Form 4 insider-selling pattern was not reviewed this cycle)
kill_criteria: Home sale gross margin falls below 22% for two consecutive quarters (vs. 25.0% in Q2 2026).
Notes payable (consolidated) rises above $2.2B (vs. $1.82B Jun-26) without a matching reduction in buyback pace.
Operating cash flow is negative for a full fiscal year (vs. +$176.8M H1 2026).
Net new order units decline YoY for two consecutive quarters (vs. +6% in Q2 2026).
key_adverse_facts: Notes payable rose from $1,631.1M (Dec-25) to $1,820.3M (Jun-26); the company issued $794.8M of new debt in H1 2026.
Operating cash flow fell to $176.8M (H1 2026) from $421.7M (H1 2025), a 58% decline, while the company still repurchased $681.2M of stock and paid $101.8M of dividends.
Home sale gross margin compressed 200bp YoY to 25.0% in Q2 2026.
data_conflicts: The Q02 triage cited 'low leverage (0.4x)' as a mitigant to the revenue downturn; this dossier finds leverage moved in the wrong direction this half (new debt issuance funding buybacks amid falling OCF) - the snapshot ratio may still be low in absolute terms, but the trend is adverse and was not visible in the triage's point-in-time framing.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for PHM (checked v1_valuation_table.csv, absent). Reverse earnings-yield Gordon-growth DCF implies ~2.3% perpetual growth at an assumed 10.5% cost of equity, below a ~4-5% base-case mid-cycle recovery growth assumption - priced for the downturn to persist near current depressed levels, not for full recovery. [Corrected 2026-10-08 (DV33): the reverse DCF treated TTM EPS as cash at an unanchored 10.5%. On TTM FCF after SBC ($1.45bn) with Ke 9.87% (Blume beta) the price implies about 3.6% a year versus a 4-5% base: in line. The H1 2026 debt issuance of $795M was largely refinancing ($601M repaid; net borrowing about $194M); the buyback shortfall was funded mainly by a $645M fall in cash. Verdict unchanged.]

PHM.scenario_basis: Base: TTM EPS $9.79, modest mid-cycle recovery plus buyback-driven share-count reduction, multiple re-rates from 12.2x to ~13x, dividend yield ~0.9%. Bear: downturn deepens, margins compress further, multiple stays ~10x. Bull: rate relief reaccelerates closings/ASP, margins recover toward 27%, multiple re-rates to ~14-15x. Cost-of-equity assumption 10.5% throughout (analyst estimate, not filed).
